page: Microsoft Azure F64as_v7 is a server instance belonging to the Fasv7 family, powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 64 physical cores and 64 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing an allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It utilizes the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and lacks local storage, relying instead on Premium Storage capabilities for remote disk operations. No GPU accelerators are present on this instance.

In benchmark evaluations, the F64as_v7 demonstrates top-tier performance, placing in the top 10% for both single-core and multi-core CPU workloads via stress-ng and Geekbench. The AMD EPYC processor's advanced instruction support, including AVX-512 and vector neural network instructions (VNNI), enables high throughput in specialized tasks such as software compilation, ray tracing, and cryptographic operations. Memory performance is also strong, with read-only cached memory bandwidth reaching top-tier levels, while uncached large-block read and write operations maintain high throughput.

Given its high clock speed and dedicated core allocation, the F64as_v7 is cost-efficient for compute-intensive workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. It delivers high throughput in multi-threaded processing tasks, database operations, and static web serving. Additionally, the instance supports medium-scale language model inference, showing strong to top-tier token generation speeds, though performance scales down to average levels for larger 70B parameter models. This makes it applicable for CI/CD pipelines, web serving, and CPU-bound data processing.
